Yes — very likely.

At 48° above the horizon, the Moon is comfortably high in the sky, and at about 89.5% illuminated it is a bright waxing/waning gibbous Moon. Even during nautical twilight, a Moon that bright should be plainly visible to normal unaided eyesight in clear conditions.

Look roughly west, azimuth 272° — essentially due west, just a little north of it — and about halfway up the sky (48° altitude). It should stand out strongly, though the brightening dawn sky near the eastern horizon will not interfere much because the Moon is on the opposite side of the sky.
